chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Jameel ibn Darraj and Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the wife of a man who has a servant for her who had been immoral, so he became needy to her milk. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Instruct her such, so she would permit her in order to make her milk to be good'.

key_terms.فَتُحَلِّلُهَا: So she would permit her (grant freedom)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a husband whose wife's servant has committed fornication and he needs her milk?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a specific legal remedy for a husband whose wife’s slave girl, having committed fornication, possesses milk needed for nourishment or healing. The Imam instructs the wife to emancipate the servant (*tuhallilah*), a act of manumission that purifies the milk, rendering it *tayyib* (pure/wholesome) for consumption. This highlights the Shia juristic view that the status of a slave girl’s freedom directly impacts the ritual purity or quality of her bodily fluids in cases of prior fornication.
